# POSIX Basic Regular Expressions, with GNU extensions.
#
# Defining property: most metacharacters are LITERAL unless preceded
# by `\`. Group is `\(...\)`, alternation is `\|`, one-or-more is
# `\+`, zero-or-one is `\?`, bounded quantifier is `\{n,m\}`. `*`,
# `.`, `^`, `$`, and `[...]` work the same as in ERE/PCRE.
#
# Char classes (`[...]`) are tokenised as one opaque match — the
# visitor parses the body using the shared char-class helper rather
# than expressing it in the grammar. The internal rules of `[...]`
# (POSIX classes, ranges, leading-`]` literal) are stateful in a way
# that's awkward to express declaratively; one regex literal + a
# focused visitor is cleaner.
#
# Rule names are stable — the visitor dispatches on them — so don't
# rename without updating `src/shell/regex/visitors/bre.ts`.

# ─── Top level ─────────────────────────────────────────────
bre = breAlternation

# ─── Alternation ───────────────────────────────────────────
# `\|` separates sequences. Empty alternatives are allowed (matches
# real BRE behaviour) by making breSequence's atom list optional.
breAlternation = breSequence + (breAltTail)*
breAltTail     = breAltSep + breSequence
breAltSep      = /\\\|/

# ─── Sequence ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# One sequence is zero or more atom-with-quantifier slots. The `*`
# (zero-or-more) is what lets `\|\|` parse as three empty
# alternatives, matching real BRE.
breSequence = (breAtomQ)*

# ─── Atom + optional quantifier suffix ─────────────────────
# Anchors aren't quantifier-eligible in real BRE (a quantifier after
# `^` is a syntax error / undefined); we accept the quantifier
# grammatically and let the visitor decide whether to attach it. In
# practice no quantifier sneaks past `^`/`$` because the visitor
# treats anchors as atoms and ignores any following quantifier slot.
breAtomQ = breAtom + breQuantSuffix?

# Order matters — most-specific first. Group (`\(`) must beat the
# generic backslash-escape rule, brackets must be tried before the
# bare literal-char fallback.
breAtom = breGroup
        | breCharClass
        | breAnchorStart
        | breAnchorEnd
        | breDot
        | breEscapedAtom
        | breLiteralChar

# ─── Group ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
breGroup      = breGroupOpen + breAlternation + breGroupClose
breGroupOpen  = /\\\(/
breGroupClose = /\\\)/

# ─── Char class — opaque token, visitor parses the body ────
# Regex anatomy:
#   \[                                  opening bracket
#   \^?                                 optional negation
#   \]?                                 optional literal `]` at position 0 (POSIX rule)
#   (?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*         body: POSIX class OR `\X` OR non-`]`
#   \]                                  closing bracket
# The POSIX-class alternative `\[:name:\]` is listed FIRST so the
# inner `]` of `[:alpha:]` doesn't terminate the outer class — without
# this special case, `[[:alpha:]]` would match only `[[:alpha:]` and
# leave the trailing `]` dangling.
breCharClass = /\[\^?\]?(?:\[:[a-z]+:\]|\\.|[^\]])*\]/

# ─── Anchors ───────────────────────────────────────────────
breAnchorStart = "^"
breAnchorEnd   = "$"

# ─── Dot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
breDot = "."

# ─── Backslash-led atoms ───────────────────────────────────
# Listed most-specific first. The visitor dispatches on the matched
# leaf node's name so it knows which kind of escape this is.
breEscapedAtom = breBackref
               | breWordBoundaryAlias
               | breWordBoundary
               | breNonWordBoundary
               | breClassDigit
               | breClassWord
               | breClassSpace
               | breClassNotDigit
               | breClassNotWord
               | breClassNotSpace
               | breControlEscape
               | breHexEscape
               | breUnicodeEscape
               | breLiteralEscape

breBackref           = /\\[1-9]/
breWordBoundaryAlias = /\\[<>]/
breWordBoundary      = /\\b/
breNonWordBoundary   = /\\B/
breClassDigit        = /\\d/
breClassNotDigit     = /\\D/
breClassWord         = /\\w/
breClassNotWord      = /\\W/
breClassSpace        = /\\s/
breClassNotSpace     = /\\S/
breControlEscape     = /\\[ntrfv0]/
breHexEscape         = /\\x[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]/
breUnicodeEscape     = /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/
# Catch-all: `\X` for any non-special X. The exclusion list mirrors
# the rules above plus the structural escapes (`\(`, `\)`, `\|`,
# `\+`, `\?`, `\{`, `\}`) which must not be swallowed here — they're
# matched at a higher level by breGroup / breAltSep / breQuant*.
breLiteralEscape = /\\[^()|+?{}<>bBdDwWsSntrfv0xu1-9]/

# ─── Literal char ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Anything that's not a metacharacter consumed elsewhere. In BRE the
# unescaped metacharacters reduce to `.`, `*`, `^`, `$`, `[`, `\` —
# everything else is a literal. We exclude `\` so the escape rules
# above can claim it.
breLiteralChar = /[^.\\\[\^$*]/

# ─── Quantifier suffix ─────────────────────────────────────
# Order matters — `\{n,m\}` and `\{n\}` must be tried before bare
# `\+`/`\?` so the brace form isn't mis-tokenised mid-stream.
breQuantSuffix = breBraceQuant
               | breStarQ
               | breBackslashPlusQ
               | breBackslashQuestionQ

breStarQ              = "*"
breBackslashPlusQ     = /\\\+\??/
breBackslashQuestionQ = /\\\?\??/
# `\{n\}` or `\{n,m\}` or `\{n,\}`. Trailing `?` for non-greedy.
breBraceQuant         = /\\\{[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]*)?\\\}\??/
